leads.title: Hospital security guards’ actions ‘did not meet’ standards says Saskatchewan Health Authority - Indigenous Watchdog
leads.automated_excerpt: # Hospital security guards’ actions ‘did not meet’ standards says Saskatchewan Health Authority. Guards recorded wheeling First Nations man out of Prince Alberta hospital and into snowbank. ***APTN News:*** The actions of security guards at the Prince Alberta Victoria Hospital – where a First Nations man was wheeled from the emergency room, across the parking lot and left in the cold – fell short of the standards set by the Saskatchewan Health Authority (SHA), according to a review of the incident. Two separate videos, recorded on Dec. 11, show security guards at the hospital pushing Brydon Lafavour across the parking lot in a wheelchair. “The review determined that the actions taken by the contracted security officers involved did not meet SHA standards or align with our values and philosophy of care,” said a statement from the SHA to APTN News. “The security officers involved are employed through a contracted security provider, and the SHA has confirmed with the provider that the officers involved are no longer permitted to work at Prince Albert Victoria Hospital or at any other SHA site or facility. “The SHA is working closely with our security provider to ensure adherence to SHA’s operational standards and philosophy of patient-centred care.”. **Family friend says man dumpted in snow outside Prince Albert hospital has had lifelong struggles**. The SHA said it met with the Prince Albert Grand Council (PAGC) to “listen and incorporate their perspectives into our response.”.
